details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has chosen two groups of network service providers (NSPs), Nexi Payments/Deutsche Telekom and Telefónica/Indra, to build the connectivity infrastructure for a potential digital euro. These NSPs will link payment service providers and national central banks to the digital euro platform, with readiness anticipated by 2029. A 12-month pilot phase is slated to begin in late 2027.
title: ECB Selects Providers for Digital Euro Development

details: Senator Bill Hagerty (R-TN) has voiced concerns that a government-issued digital dollar could infringe upon financial freedom. This comes as federal law already restricts the Federal Reserve from issuing a retail CBDC until December 31, 2030, while the US also prepares new regulations for privately issued stablecoins.
title: Senator Hagerty Warns US CBDC Threatens Financial Freedom

details: A recent selloff in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks could potentially ease inflationary pressures and reduce upward pressure on US interest rates, according to BMO Capital Markets' Jennifer Lee. This development could impact crypto markets through a decrease in overall risk appetite, but conversely, lower interest rates might make Bitcoin and Ethereum relatively more attractive compared to traditional bonds and cash.
sourceName: KuCoin (citing BMO Capital Markets via Bloomberg)
title: AI Stock Declines May Aid Fed's Inflation Fight, Affecting Crypto

details: This week is packed with significant events, including the US midterm elections, crucial labor market reports (such as job openings and October payrolls), and major tech company earnings. These factors are expected to influence the direction of Bitcoin and the broader cryptocurrency market, potentially shaping crypto regulations and Federal Reserve interest rate expectations.
title: US Midterms, Jobs Data, Tech Earnings to Impact Crypto Markets
